claims.claim: Stream RAG issues PARTIAL tool queries during ongoing speech (before the user finishes) to mask API latency; store = 100k CRAG web docs + a simulated KG API, retrieval is over TEXT, query = model-generated tool-query text from partial ASR, injection = concat refs then a spoken-summary fusion; a post-training pipeline teaches when-to-trigger + summary generation (negative sampling p=0.1 for error recovery). Gains: closed→open book 11.1%→26.3% abs (Qwen2.5-7B, 140% rel); model-triggered streaming 34.2% abs (200% rel); tool latency -20% (synthetic 20.7%, human 53.4%). Base models Qwen-OMNI, OpusLM, Kimi-Audio.
claims.source: Stream RAG: Instant and Accurate Spoken Dialogue Systems with Streaming Tool Usage, arXiv:2510.02044, 2025 [fetched]
claims.relevance: Direct analog to our mock retrieval pipeline + step-3 RL: 'when to retrieve' and 'how to fuse' are exactly the RL-tunable levers, but they achieve it by POST-TRAINING weights — the training-free slot is open.

claims.claim: AudioCRAG is the spoken-RAG benchmark built by converting CRAG's 2,706 text queries to speech: AudioCRAG-Synthetic = 1,862 TTS queries filtered (Whisper WER=0, UTMOS>=3.5), AudioCRAG-Human = 618 human recordings; 569 queries rewritten for naturalness.
claims.source: Stream RAG, arXiv:2510.02044, 2025 [fetched]
claims.relevance: A ready spoken-RAG testbed (English QA); positions what a speech-keyed KB eval looks like, and what it does NOT cover (no paralinguistic/speaker/emotion-keyed retrieval).

claims.claim: End-to-end S2S RAG on GLM-4-Voice embeds speech queries and text documents into ONE shared space via a FROZEN SONAR speech encoder (no fine-tuning), enabling direct speech->text retrieval; retrieved text is concatenated with the spoken query and fed to the frozen S2S model. Gains: +~20% HotpotQA, +~43% RGB-zh; retrieval time 0.4s->0.08s (1/4).
claims.source: Enhancing Speech-to-Speech Dialogue Modeling with End-to-End Retrieval-Augmented Generation, arXiv:2505.00028, EMNLP Findings 2025 [fetched]
claims.relevance: Frozen-encoder shared-space direct speech->text retrieval is exactly our key-org option; likely the 'GLM-Voice-RAG' already in our records — position newer work against it, don't recount as novel.

claims.claim: Omni-Embed-Nemotron is a unified bi-encoder over text/image/audio/video on the Qwen2.5-Omni-3B Thinker backbone; audio+visual encoders are FROZEN, only a LoRA head (r=16, alpha=32) on the LLM is trained; audio can be BOTH a query and a stored document; benchmarks FineVideo 0.5662 NDCG@10, ViDoRe 85.7 nDCG@5, MTEB 0.6059.
claims.source: Omni-Embed-Nemotron: A Unified Multimodal Retrieval Model for Text, Image, Audio, and Video, arXiv:2510.03458, 2025 [fetched]
claims.relevance: Candidate KEY encoder for our faiss KB (audio as document); confirms the frozen-encoder + light-head recipe. Already flagged in our records (asymmetric encode_document, NC license) — position, note license risk.

claims.claim: Audiopedia's r-AQA sub-task retrieves relevant AUDIO samples then answers; the knowledge store is Wikidata triplets (TextKVQA business-KB), and Audio Entity Linking transcribes audio (wav2vec2), encodes it, and cosine-matches to entity embeddings to fetch the linked knowledge; fully zero-shot/FROZEN (LTU-AS s-AQA 3.9%->54.7%). Sizes: s-AQA 14,702 / m-AQA 500 / r-AQA 115.
claims.source: Audiopedia: Audio QA with Knowledge, arXiv:2412.20619, Dec 2024 [fetched]
claims.relevance: Knowledge-injection-into-frozen-audio-model benchmark using entity-linked KG values — a value-org (KG triplet) + entity-key option; borderline pre-window (Dec 2024) but the canonical 'AQA with knowledge' reference.

claims.claim: SpeechT-RAG keys retrieval on speech TIMING/prosodic features (non-lexical) rather than transcript text for depression detection, and reports comparable accuracy to a FINE-TUNED LLM WITHOUT any additional training, plus a confidence score derived from the same temporal features.
claims.source: SpeechT-RAG: Reliable Depression Detection in LLMs with RAG Using Speech Timing Information, arXiv:2502.10950, ACL Findings 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Proof that a paralinguistic (non-lexical) retrieval KEY works and that a training-free RAG can match fine-tuning — directly supports our key-org (non-lexical) and training-free thesis.

claims.claim: LongAudio-RAG (LA-RAG) grounds LLM answers in retrieved, TIMESTAMPED acoustic-event detections (structured records) rather than raw audio, using structured/event-level retrieval that beats vanilla RAG and text-to-SQL for multi-hour audio QA.
claims.source: LongAudio-RAG: Event-Grounded Question Answering over Multi-Hour Long Audio, arXiv:2602.14612, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Value-org option = structured timestamped-event store; retrieval-strategy option = structured/SQL over events. Note: shares the 'LA-RAG' abbreviation with a distinct token-level ASR datastore paper — disambiguate.

claims.claim: PlanRAG-Audio plans WHICH modalities and temporal spans a query needs, then retrieves only query-relevant info from a structured text+audio DB, decoupling inference cost from raw audio length; the plan specifies required representations, per-stream filters, joins, returned fields, and output schema.
claims.source: PlanRAG-Audio: Planning and Retrieval Augmented Generation for Long-form Audio Understanding, arXiv:2605.20414, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Query-construction option = LLM retrieval-planning; an RL-tunable policy slot (plan-then-retrieve) for step-3.

claims.claim: VoiceAgentRAG (Salesforce) uses a dual-agent design: a background Slow Thinker predicts likely follow-ups and prefetches document chunks into a FAISS-backed semantic cache; a foreground Fast Talker reads only the sub-millisecond cache; 75% cache-hit rate, ~316x retrieval-latency reduction to meet the 200ms voice budget.
claims.source: VoiceAgentRAG: Solving the RAG Latency Bottleneck in Real-Time Voice Agents Using Dual-Agent Architectures, arXiv:2603.02206, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Retrieval-strategy option = predictive semantic cache over faiss (same stack as ours); a latency lever orthogonal to accuracy.

claims.claim: A conversational-emotion-recognition study retrieves in-context EXEMPLARS via Augmented Example Retrieval (AER): LLM paraphrases each reference utterance, SentenceTransformer-encodes them, cosine-matches the target, and picks additional examples covering remaining emotions; AER consistently beats other ICL retrieval on IEMOCAP/MELD/EmoryNLP.
claims.source: How to Retrieve Examples in In-context Learning to Improve Conversational Emotion Recognition using LLMs?, arXiv:2506.20199, 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Directly the EXEMPLAR grain in our KB and a query-construction (paraphrase-augmented) option; emotion axis is a W4 disentangle target.

claims.claim: 'Hearing More with Less' augments conversational LLM-based ASR with MULTIMODAL retrieval-AND-SELECTION: it retrieves historical audio segments + their transcripts, then applies a selection module to filter candidates before prompt injection.
claims.source: Hearing More with Less: Multi-Modal Retrieval-and-Selection Augmented Conversational LLM-Based ASR, arXiv:2508.01166, 2025 [fetched-partial]
claims.relevance: Primitive = a selection/filter stage after retrieval (retrieve-then-select), and retrieval over the model's OWN conversational history.

claims.claim: RASST does retrieval-augmented SIMULTANEOUS speech translation: a lightweight speech-text retriever produces chunkwise terminology hints via multi-scale retrieval from a text glossary under streaming constraints, and the Speech-LLM is trained to decide whether/when to apply each term; +~40% terminology accuracy, up to +3 BLEU, negligible overhead.
claims.source: RASST: Retrieval-Augmented Simultaneous Speech Translation, arXiv:2601.22777, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Cross-modal glossary retrieval + streaming 'whether/when to apply retrieved item' = a delivery/gating lever; content(ST) axis is a W4 target.

claims.claim: M3KG-RAG builds a multi-hop MULTIMODAL knowledge graph via a lightweight multi-agent pipeline and does modality-wise retrieval for audio-visual reasoning in MLLMs, explicitly to overcome retrieval limited to similarity in a shared multimodal embedding space.
claims.source: M3KG-RAG: Multi-hop Multimodal Knowledge Graph-enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation, arXiv:2512.20136, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Value-org = MMKG and retrieval-strategy = graph/subgraph multi-hop over audio-visual; high build cost on our stack.

claims.claim: SceneRAG segments long video into narrative-consistent scenes by fusing vision+audio+subtitle (ASR transcripts + temporal metadata) and indexes scenes in a vector DB for scene-level retrieval.
claims.source: SceneRAG: Scene-level Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Video Understanding, arXiv:2506.07600, 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Value-org = scene/segment units from spoken content; shows spoken-content-derived chunking as a store-organization choice.

claims.claim: AFA uses VOICE EMBEDDINGS to identify who is speaking (Speaker-ID) and maintains identity-aware memory to prevent persona confusion across multiple users sharing one device.
claims.source: AFA: Identity-Aware Memory for Preventing Persona Confusion in Multi-User Dialogue, arXiv:2604.25022, 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Speaker-ID voiceprint as the retrieval KEY into a memory store = exactly our speech-vector key + memory grain; W4 speaker-ID axis.

claims.claim: CarMem gives LLM voice assistants long-term memory via CATEGORY-BOUNDING: it retrieves semantically relevant user preferences and, before insertion, compares to existing ones applying append/pass/update maintenance operations.
claims.source: CarMem: Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLM Voice Assistants through Category-Bounding, arXiv:2501.09645, 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Memory-grain value-org with explicit maintenance ops (append/pass/update) — a store-lifecycle design our KB lacks.

claims.claim: Mem-PAL introduces H2Memory, a hierarchical and heterogeneous memory framework for modeling, retrieving, and updating diverse interaction histories in personalized dialogue assistants.
claims.source: Mem-PAL: Towards Memory-based Personalized Dialogue Assistants for Long-term User-Agent Interaction, arXiv:2511.13410, 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Value-org = hierarchical/heterogeneous memory; positions newer episodic-memory work against the mem0/MemGPT line already in our records.

claims.claim: AudioRAG+ performs FEEDBACK-DRIVEN retrieval-augmented audio GENERATION with large audio-language models, iterating retrieval based on generation feedback.
claims.source: AudioRAG+: Feedback-driven Retrieval-augmented Audio Generation with Large Audio Language Models, arXiv:2511.01091, 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Retrieval-strategy = iterative feedback/rerank loop, an RL-adjacent lever (reward = generation quality).

claims.claim: The Multimodal-RAG survey's audio-centric section lists exactly RECAST, WavRAG, SpeechRAG, SEAL, and contextual-ASR-with-RAG (no audio-RAG benchmarks), and the June-2025 enhanced version added agentic-interaction and audio-centric retrieval as new topics.
claims.source: Ask in Any Modality: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal RAG (llm-lab-org/Multimodal-RAG-Survey), 2025 [fetched]
claims.relevance: Confirms our prior-art list is exhaustive for the survey's audio section; the newest 2026 systems (Stream RAG, PlanRAG-Audio, LongAudio-RAG, VoiceAgentRAG, RASST) are NOT yet catalogued there — our positioning is ahead of the survey.

claims.claim: Spoken-QA/omni benchmarks published 2025-2026 that can serve as RAG testbeds include SpokenNativQA (~33k multilingual everyday spoken Q&A, arXiv:2505.19163), TELEVAL (Chinese interactive SLM benchmark, arXiv:2507.18061), OmniEval (visual+auditory+textual omni benchmark, arXiv:2506.20960), and DCASE-2025 Task-5 AQA (arXiv:2505.07365).
claims.source: SpokenNativQA (2505.19163); TELEVAL (2507.18061); OmniEval (2506.20960); DCASE2025-AQA (2505.07365), 2025 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Candidate eval sets; note NONE evaluate retrieval keyed on paralinguistic/speaker/emotion axes — a benchmark gap for our KB.

claims.claim: Audio-native FUNCTION-CALLING benchmarks now exist (BFCL-Audio from Salesforce/Berkeley; Audio2Tool 'Speak, Call, Act', arXiv:2604.22821), mapping raw speech directly to executable API/tool calls.
claims.source: Audio2Tool: Speak, Call, Act, arXiv:2604.22821, 2026; BFCL-Audio [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Positions retrieval-as-a-tool for a frozen speech model; a delivery/agentic framing for step-3 (retrieval as one callable tool).

claims.claim: Security work on multimodal RAG covers Caption-Poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented text-to-MUSIC generation (arXiv:2605.30365) and membership-inference / image-caption-retrieval attacks on multimodal RAG (arXiv:2601.17644), but no speech-keyed-KB poisoning study.
claims.source: Mental Damage: Caption Poisoning on RA Text-to-Music (2605.30365); Do Multimodal RAG Systems Leak Data? (2601.17644), 2026 [search-snippet]
claims.relevance: Robustness/attack-surface gap: speech-vector-keyed KB poisoning is unstudied — a differentiator/risk to flag.

candidates.name: Audio-native joint speech-text embedding key (utterance-level)
candidates.what: Utterance-level speech embedding placed in a shared space with text so a spoken query retrieves text values directly, no ASR. Seen in WavRAG/SpeechRAG/SEAL and the frozen-SONAR GLM-4-Voice S2S-RAG.
candidates.evidence: E2E S2S RAG frozen SONAR shared-space (arXiv:2505.00028); survey audio section (llm-lab-org).

candidates.name: Paralinguistic / timing-feature retrieval key
candidates.what: Key the index on non-lexical prosodic/timing vectors instead of transcript text; retrieves exemplars sharing acoustic-temporal signature.
candidates.evidence: SpeechT-RAG training-free depression detection with speech-timing keys (arXiv:2502.10950).

candidates.name: Speaker-ID voiceprint key
candidates.what: Use a speaker/voice embedding as the key so retrieval is scoped by identity; pairs naturally with a per-speaker memory store.
candidates.evidence: AFA identity-aware memory via voice embeddings (arXiv:2604.25022); our KB is already speech-keyed.

candidates.name: Entity-linked key (audio->entity->KG node)
candidates.what: Transcribe/encode audio, link to a named entity, and key retrieval on the entity node in a KG.
candidates.evidence: Audiopedia Audio Entity Linking over Wikidata business-KB (arXiv:2412.20619).

candidates.name: Audio+text hybrid value representation
candidates.what: Store each knowledge item as a unified audio+text object so retrieved evidence carries both the waveform and its transcript/metadata.
candidates.evidence: WavRAG unified audio-text knowledge representation (survey; arXiv:2502.14727, prior art — position only).

candidates.name: KG-triplet / multimodal-KG value store
candidates.what: Values are Wikidata-style triplets or a multi-hop multimodal knowledge graph enabling compositional/subgraph evidence.
candidates.evidence: Audiopedia triplets (2412.20619); M3KG-RAG MMKG for audio-visual (arXiv:2512.20136).

candidates.name: Timestamped acoustic-event / structured records
candidates.what: Store structured, timestamped event detections (who/what/when) instead of raw audio; retrieval is event-level and joinable.
candidates.evidence: LongAudio-RAG event-grounded structured retrieval (arXiv:2602.14612).

candidates.name: Labeled exemplar store (paralinguistic labels)
candidates.what: Values are labeled example utterances (emotion/style/intent) fetched as in-context demonstrations for a frozen reader.
candidates.evidence: AER exemplar retrieval for conversational emotion recognition (arXiv:2506.20199) — matches our 'exemplar' grain.

candidates.name: Speaker-keyed episodic memory with maintenance ops
candidates.what: Per-user memory values with explicit append/pass/update lifecycle and hierarchical structure.
candidates.evidence: CarMem category-bounding + maintenance ops (arXiv:2501.09645); Mem-PAL H2Memory (arXiv:2511.13410) — matches our 'memory' grain.

candidates.name: Scene/segment units from spoken content
candidates.what: Chunk long audio/video into narrative-consistent segments (via ASR+temporal cues) as the retrievable value unit.
candidates.evidence: SceneRAG scene segmentation fusing audio+subtitle (arXiv:2506.07600).

candidates.name: Frozen-encoder bi-encoder dense retrieval + light head
candidates.what: Encode query and document with frozen omni encoders, add only a small trained/pooling head; audio usable as query and document.
candidates.evidence: Omni-Embed-Nemotron frozen audio/visual encoders + LoRA head on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B (arXiv:2510.03458).

candidates.name: ASR-then-text cascade retrieval (baseline)
candidates.what: Transcribe with the frozen model, retrieve over a text index; simplest, highest-fidelity-per-token but drops acoustic info.
candidates.evidence: Ubiquitous baseline that WavRAG/SpeechRAG report ~8-14x slower yet comparable recall vs audio-native (arXiv:2502.14727).

candidates.name: Structured / text-to-SQL retrieval over events
candidates.what: Compile the query into a structured plan/SQL over a typed event+text DB rather than top-k dense lookup.
candidates.evidence: LongAudio-RAG (2602.14612) and PlanRAG-Audio structured DB (arXiv:2605.20414).

candidates.name: Graph / subgraph multi-hop retrieval
candidates.what: Traverse a knowledge graph for path/subgraph evidence supporting multi-hop audio-visual questions.
candidates.evidence: M3KG-RAG modality-wise multi-hop retrieval (arXiv:2512.20136).

candidates.name: Streaming / predictive mid-utterance retrieval
candidates.what: Issue partial retrieval queries before the user finishes speaking to hide latency; a reflector evaluates cached intermediate queries.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG fixed-interval + model-triggered streaming (arXiv:2510.02044).

candidates.name: Dual-agent predictive semantic cache (faiss)
candidates.what: A background agent predicts follow-ups and prefetches into a faiss semantic cache; the foreground reader hits the cache in sub-ms.
candidates.evidence: VoiceAgentRAG 75% hit / 316x latency cut on FAISS (arXiv:2603.02206) — same faiss stack as ours.

candidates.name: Feedback-driven / iterative retrieval loop
candidates.what: Re-retrieve conditioned on the reader's generation feedback until a quality criterion is met.
candidates.evidence: AudioRAG+ feedback-driven RA audio generation (arXiv:2511.01091).

candidates.name: Retrieve-then-select (two-stage filter)
candidates.what: Over-retrieve candidates then apply a selection module to pick the few actually injected.
candidates.evidence: Hearing More with Less retrieval-and-selection (arXiv:2508.01166).

candidates.name: Model-generated tool query from audio
candidates.what: Frozen reader emits a text tool-query maximizing P(query|audio) rather than using the raw transcript as the query.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG P(Q^T|Q) tool-query generation (arXiv:2510.02044).

candidates.name: Retrieval planning (modality + temporal span)
candidates.what: LLM first plans which modalities/spans/filters are needed, then retrieves only those — an explicit, RL-tunable plan policy.
candidates.evidence: PlanRAG-Audio retrieval plan schema (arXiv:2605.20414).

candidates.name: Paraphrase-augmented exemplar query
candidates.what: Generate paraphrases of the reference/target to build a more robust exemplar-retrieval query for paralinguistic labels.
candidates.evidence: AER paraphrase-augmented retrieval (arXiv:2506.20199).

candidates.name: Multi-scale chunkwise glossary query (streaming)
candidates.what: Form retrieval queries at multiple granularities per speech chunk to fetch terminology hints under streaming constraints.
candidates.evidence: RASST multi-scale chunkwise terminology retrieval (arXiv:2601.22777).

candidates.name: Concat-refs + chain-of-thought injection
candidates.what: Inject retrieved evidence as concatenated references and prompt the frozen reader with CoT to use them.
candidates.evidence: WavRAG CoT-enhanced in-context injection (arXiv:2502.14727, prior art — baseline delivery).

candidates.name: Spoken-summary fusion of audio query + retrieved text
candidates.what: Have the reader produce a spoken summary that fuses the original audio query with retrieved text results.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG response generation P(A|Q,R) as spoken summary (arXiv:2510.02044).

candidates.name: In-context labeled exemplars for paralinguistics
candidates.what: Deliver retrieved labeled examples (emotion/style) as few-shot demonstrations to steer a frozen reader's paralinguistic judgment.
candidates.evidence: AER in-context emotion exemplars beating other ICL (arXiv:2506.20199).

candidates.name: Whether/when-to-apply retrieved-item gate
candidates.what: A decision head that gates each retrieved item (apply/skip) at delivery time, learned or reward-tuned.
candidates.evidence: RASST learns whether/when to apply each retrieved term (arXiv:2601.22777); relates to prior-art TARG/NEST gating line.

candidates.name: Selection / reranker primitive
candidates.what: A standalone module that scores and filters retrieved candidates before injection.
candidates.evidence: Hearing More with Less selection module (arXiv:2508.01166).

candidates.name: Reflector primitive (evaluate cached queries)
candidates.what: A module that inspects cached intermediate/partial queries and decides whether to keep, refine, or re-trigger.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG reflector module (arXiv:2510.02044).

candidates.name: Confidence/uncertainty scorer from retrieval features
candidates.what: Derive a calibrated confidence from the same features used for retrieval (e.g., timing), for abstention/trust.
candidates.evidence: SpeechT-RAG confidence scoring from temporal features (arXiv:2502.10950).

candidates.name: Grain-router primitive (knowledge/memory/exemplar)
candidates.what: A router that decides which grain of the co-indexed store to query for a given request; NOT present in any surveyed single-grain system.
candidates.evidence: Gap synthesis: WavRAG=knowledge, CarMem/AFA=memory, AER=exemplar each pick ONE grain; combining+routing is unoccupied.

candidates.name: Training-free RL over when/whether-to-retrieve gate
candidates.what: Replace Stream-RAG/RASST post-training with reward-guided, inference-time optimization of the retrieval trigger on a FROZEN reader.
candidates.evidence: Stream RAG (2510.02044) and RASST (2601.22777) get this via weight updates; the training-free slot is open (our thesis).

candidates.name: RL best-of-N reranking of retrieved candidates
candidates.what: Use an omni-verifier reward to rerank/select among retrieved candidates at inference, no weight change.
candidates.evidence: Fits W1 best-of-N machinery; Hearing-More selection (2508.01166) and AudioRAG+ feedback (2511.01091) motivate reward-guided selection.

candidates.name: RL-tuned retrieval-planning policy (weights frozen)
candidates.what: Reward-guide the plan-then-retrieve policy (which modality/span/filter) without training the model.
candidates.evidence: PlanRAG-Audio (2605.20414) supplies the plan action-space; training-free control of it is unexplored.

gaps:
EXPLICIT GAPS (what no surveyed 2025-2026 system covers, that our program needs):
1) TRAINING-FREE-RL ON A FROZEN READER is unoccupied. Every accuracy-lever system either trains a retriever (WavRAG, SEAL, BR-ASR, Omni-Embed-Nemotron LoRA) or POST-TRAINS the reader (Stream RAG, RASST). SpeechT-RAG is the only training-free RAG that matches fine-tuning, but it has no RL/reward-guided retrieval control. Our step-3 (reward-guided, inference-time retrieval on a frozen Qwen3-Omni-30B) is genuinely novel vs the surveyed field.
2) GRAIN-TAGGED UNIFIED STORE is unbuilt. Each system commits to ONE grain: WavRAG/SpeechRAG/Audiopedia = knowledge; CarMem/AFA/Mem-PAL = memory; AER = exemplar. No system co-indexes knowledge+memory+exemplar in one speech-keyed index or ROUTES by grain — a clean differentiator (candidate 'grain-router primitive').
3) NON-LEXICAL KEYS BEYOND TIMING/SPEAKER are absent. Only SpeechT-RAG keys on timing and AFA on voiceprint. NO surveyed system keys retrieval on EMOTION/SER or LANGUAGE/INTENT embeddings — exactly W4's disentangled axes — leaving the whole 'retrieve by paralinguistic/semantic axis' space open.
4) WORD-LEVEL (vs utterance-level) speech-vector keys for open-domain KNOWLEDGE injection do not exist; word/token-level speech retrieval is confined to ASR adaptation (kNN-CTC/token-datastore prior art), not knowledge grounding of a frozen omni reader.
5) BENCHMARK GAP: spoken-RAG evals (AudioCRAG, SpokenNativQA, Audiopedia r-AQA, TELEVAL) are lexical QA in EN/ZH; none evaluate retrieval keyed on speaker/emotion/paralinguistic axes, and none test grain-routing correctness. No benchmark matches our KB's evaluation needs.
6) STACK-TRANSFER RISK: every surveyed system assumes HF/vLLM or a trainable encoder; none demonstrate the frozen-GGUF-reader (llama.cpp) + external-faiss pattern we run. Open engineering question: extracting hidden states / latent keys from llama.cpp for latent-keyed retrieval (our audit_source latent path).
7) ROBUSTNESS unstudied for speech: poisoning/membership-inference exist only for text-to-music and image-caption RAG (2605.30365, 2601.17644); speech-vector-keyed KB poisoning/leakage is a blank.
8) RETRIEVAL OVER THE MODEL'S OWN OUTPUTS for knowledge (not just ASR history as in Hearing-More-with-Less) — self-grounding a frozen omni against its own prior generations — is unexplored.
DISAMBIGUATION NOTE: two distinct systems share the 'LA-RAG' abbreviation — LongAudio-RAG (event-grounded long-audio QA, 2602.14612) and the older token-level speech-datastore LA-RAG for ASR accent adaptation (kNN-line prior art); keep them separate. The E2E S2S RAG paper (2505.00028, GLM-4-Voice + frozen SONAR) is very likely the 'GLM-Voice-RAG' already in our records — treated as prior-art overlap, not double-counted as novel.
COVERAGE NOTE: many 2026 items (arXiv 2601-2606) were read via search-result snippets only, not full-text fetch — marked [search-snippet] in sources; fetched-full-text items marked [fetched]. Prior-art items (WavRAG, SpeechRAG, SEAL, RECAST, BR-ASR, MARS, VoxRAG, GLM-Voice-RAG, kNN/M2R-Whisper/kNN-CTC line, TARG/NEST gating, mem0/MemGPT) were NOT re-surveyed — only positioned.
